# Results — Study 122 (Gross-Profitability) on real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — annual sort on
GrossProfit / Assets (GP/A), long top quintile vs short bottom quintile, equal-weight,
one-year reporting lag — measured against the equal-weight universe on the current S&P 500
universe projected backwards. As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Signal (GrossProfit / Assets) | 20 years x 213 tickers | `210f5cf55902` |
| Forward returns | 20 years x 420 tickers | `c36c64f964b2` |
| Years covered | 2006 – 2025 | — |

**Sources:** EDGAR XBRL shared caches (`_edgar_GrossProfit.parquet`, `_edgar_Assets.parquet`);
annual returns from `_edgar_yrret.parquet` (Yahoo Finance monthly prices, calendar-year
compounded). Universe: current S&P 500 membership, survivorship-biased. Signal years with
fewer than 20 firms are dropped; 2026 (partial) is excluded.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the universe is the current S&P 500 membership
projected backwards. All positive results should be read as **upper-bound estimates**;
the true population effect is likely smaller and possibly absent.

## The honest test — top vs bottom GP/A quintile, annual rebalance

Signal in year *y* = GrossProfit_y / Assets_y. Strategy buys the signal at year-*y* close
(or equivalently at Jan 1 of year *y+1*, after full reporting delay) and measures the return
during calendar year *y+1*.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N years | 18 (2008–2025) |
| Mean hedge return | **+3.28%/yr** |
| Vol | 16.52%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | +0.199 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+0.803** |
| Hit rate (years > 0) | 61.1% |
| Max drawdown | −45.8% |

- The hedge earns **+3.28%/yr** at HAC *t* = **+0.803** — well below the inference bar of
  |*t*| ≥ 2. The effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero at conventional
  significance levels.
- The high-GP/A leg earns **+19.3%/yr** vs the equal-weight market at **+21.5%/yr** —
  the long leg actually **underperforms** the market by **−2.2%/yr** on this survivor panel.
- The low-GP/A leg earns **+16.0%/yr**, underperforming the market by **−5.5%/yr**.
- The hedge is positive in 11/18 years (61%); the two most recent years (2024, 2025) were
  **−25%** and **−27%**, suggesting the signal has reversed recently on large-cap survivors.

## Legs vs equal-weight market

| Leg | Mean return | vs market |
|---|--:|--:|
| High GP/A (top quintile) | +19.27%/yr | −2.21%/yr |
| Low GP/A (bottom quintile) | +15.99%/yr | −5.49%/yr |
| **Hedge (high − low)** | **+3.28%/yr** | — |
| Equal-weight market | +21.48%/yr | 0 |

Note: both legs trail the equal-weight market. This is a selection artefact of
survivorship bias: large-cap survivors outperform broadly, but the top GP/A firms within
that already-survivor universe are not the best performers.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Hedge HAC *t* = +0.803 (|t| < 2). A positive mean (+3.3%/yr) is
  consistent with the literature but falls below the inference bar on this short,
  survivorship-biased panel. Literature support (Novy-Marx 2013) upgrades this from NONE
  to WEAK, but the real-tape numbers alone do not clear the bar.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The hedge has negative Sharpe in 8 of 18 years, a max
  drawdown of −46%, and the most recent two years reversed sharply. Annual turnover is
  manageable, but the signal is too noisy on a large-cap survivor panel to trade
  confidently. A broader, non-biased universe (e.g. full Russell 3000) would be needed to
  assess real tradability.
- **Survivorship caveat:** the current S&P 500 panel biases results upward. The true
  population hedge (including delisted firms) is likely smaller; the recent reversals may
  be partly a mean-reversion of the selection premium.
